question: Given componentDidMount() and componentDidUpdate(prevProps), why might fetching data in both create race conditions? async componentDidMount() { const data = await fetch(...); this.setState({ data }); }
options: Multiple concurrent fetches may complete out-of-order, setting stale data
componentDidMount only runs once, race condition is impossible
componentDidUpdate is never called after mount
Race conditions only occur with useEffect, not lifecycle methods
explanation: If componentDidUpdate also fetches and requests complete out-of-order, the older response may overwrite the newer one; use AbortController or cleanup flags.

question: Why is componentWillUnmount the place to clean up subscriptions? componentWillUnmount() { this.subscription.unsubscribe(); }
options: It's the last method called before the component is removed from DOM
componentDidMount is too early to set up, so cleanup is in unmount
Cleanup must happen synchronously before render
It prevents memory leaks from persisting after unmount
explanation: componentWillUnmount is called right before the component is removed; cleanup here frees resources (subscriptions, timers) that would otherwise persist.

question: Given componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState), why doesn't this always fire when props change? const shouldUpdate = (nextProps) => false;
options: shouldComponentUpdate returning false skips the update and componentDidUpdate
componentDidUpdate always fires regardless of shouldComponentUpdate
Props changes automatically trigger componentDidUpdate
shouldComponentUpdate is for performance only, not control flow
explanation: If shouldComponentUpdate returns false, the component doesn't re-render, so componentDidUpdate never fires; this prevents bugs from stale updates.

question: Why might getDerivedStateFromProps be dangerous for syncing state and props? static getDerivedStateFromProps(props, state) { return props; }
options: It runs every render, overwriting state and making it uncontrollable
It never runs, props and state are always separate
It's safe and the recommended way to sync props to state
It only runs during mount, not updates
explanation: getDerivedStateFromProps runs on every render; overwriting state from props makes the component uncontrolled and removes ability to edit state.

question: Given multiple setState calls in componentDidMount, why might the final render use stale state? componentDidMount() { this.setState({ x: 1 }); this.setState({ y: 2 }); }
options: setState is batched, so both complete before re-render
setState calls are asynchronous and may apply out-of-order
Both setState calls merge, resulting in { x: 1, y: 2 }
componentDidMount prevents any state updates
explanation: In a lifecycle method, setState calls are batched; the component re-renders once with both updates applied, not out-of-order.

question: Why is componentDidMount a better place for data fetching than componentWillMount? componentWillMount() { this.fetchData(); }
options: componentWillMount runs before mount, fetch completes after render
componentWillMount is removed; componentDidMount is the safe alternative
componentWillMount is synchronous, blocking initial render
Fetching in willMount triggers unnecessary re-renders
explanation: componentWillMount is deprecated (removed in React 18); componentDidMount runs after render, ensuring the component can safely set state.

question: Given componentDidUpdate(prevProps) { if (prevProps.id !== this.props.id) this.fetchData(); }, why might this cause infinite loops with siblings?
options: Fetching may update parent state, re-rendering siblings and re-triggering fetch
componentDidUpdate only runs once per mount
Fetching in componentDidUpdate is not allowed
This pattern is safe and never causes loops
explanation: If fetching updates parent state and re-renders other siblings, their prop changes may trigger their updates, creating a cascade loop.

question: Why does React call render() multiple times during the render phase? Why shouldn't render have side effects?
options: render is pure; side effects may run multiple times or be abandoned
render is guaranteed to run once per lifecycle
render never re-runs, each return is final
Side effects in render are necessary for data fetching
explanation: React may render a component multiple times (especially with Suspense or error boundaries) or abandon a render; side effects run N times, breaking consistency.

question: Given a component that logs in multiple lifecycle methods, what is the typical order? componentWillMount -> componentDidMount -> componentDidUpdate -> componentWillUnmount
options: willMount, didMount, didUpdate, willUnmount (in lifecycle order)
didMount, willMount, willUnmount, didUpdate (out of order)
All run simultaneously
Only didMount runs, others are skipped
explanation: willMount (deprecated, skipped in React 18) -> render -> didMount (once) -> didUpdate (on prop/state change) -> willUnmount (before removal).

question: Why might a component with children not re-render when only a child's internal state changes? Why is key important for list items?
options: Parent only re-renders if parent's own state/props change, child state is isolated
Parent always re-renders when any child state changes
Children cannot have state, only parents can
Key prevents any re-renders regardless of state
explanation: Parent doesn't re-render based on child state; key matters for list identity so React matches the same component instance across re-renders.
